title: Case: Recipient waiting at home asks whether an international parcel is arriving today
context: DL-923, a replacement boiler unit for an espresso machine, is travelling from a seller in Halvenmark through Tressia to a recipient in Norrow. The recipient account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request: Fifty minutes on hold to be told it isn't even in Tressia yet, never mind here. Your own page STILL says arriving today, I'm looking at it right now. I took a day's leave for this and I've sat in the house since seven like an idiot. So which is it? Is it coming today or is your website talking absolute crap? One straight bloody answer from somebody who actually knows where the thing is. And don't read me the tracking page, I can read.

events.body: DL-923: the public tracking page shows 'Estimated delivery: today, 12 May'. That estimate is produced automatically from the service level at booking. We have not reviewed the scan history for this shipment.
Page says today. I've taken the day off to be in. Roughly what time?

Network notice, all desks: the Halvenmark to Tressia trunk is running two to four days behind this week. This is a general notice and is not a statement about any one shipment. Where an individual international parcel actually is gets confirmed by Parcel trace team, by email.

events.from: Customer care line, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: Agent: Sorry for the wait. The last scan I can see on DL-923 is departure from the Halvenmark export hub on 8 May. Caller: The page says it's arriving today. Agent: I can see that. I've got nothing in Tressia and nothing at the Norrow border. Caller: So it hasn't left Halvenmark? Agent: I can't say that either, I only see the scans on my screen and I'm told there can be others I don't see. Caller: Then is it coming today or not? Agent: I can't tell you. I don't know why the page says today.

Fifty minutes on hold to be told it isn't even in Tressia yet, never mind here. Your own page STILL says arriving today, I'm looking at it right now. I took a day's leave for this and I've sat in the house since seven like an idiot. So which is it? Is it coming today or is your website talking absolute crap? One straight bloody answer from somebody who actually knows where the thing is. And don't read me the tracking page, I can read.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Plover Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Sets out the conflict on DL-923 between the page's 'today' estimate and the care line's last visible scan of 8 May at the Halvenmark export hub, and asks where the parcel is and what the realistic estimate is.

must: Puts both sources to Parcel trace team as an unresolved conflict: the public page shows estimated delivery today, 12 May; the care line agent could see no scan after departure from the Halvenmark export hub on 8 May and said there may be scans not visible to them.
Asks Parcel trace team to confirm where DL-923 actually is and whether delivery today is possible, and to give a realistic estimate.
Tells Parcel trace team that the recipient has taken a day's leave and is waiting at home today on the strength of the page, so a reply is needed today.
must_not: Tells the recipient the parcel is arriving today, or repeats the tracking page estimate to him.
Tells the recipient as settled fact that the parcel is still in Halvenmark or will not come today.
Turns the general two to four day trunk delay into a new delivery date for this parcel.
Replies to the recipient with a line about estimates not being guaranteed, or comments on his language, without getting him an answer.
expected.reference_message: DL-923, Halvenmark to Norrow via Tressia, recipient Tobin Achterberg: I need to know where this parcel actually is, today. Two sources disagree. The public tracking page shows 'Estimated delivery: today, 12 May'; Tracking support say that figure is automatic from the booked service level. The care line told the recipient at 11:45 that the last scan they can see is departure from the Halvenmark export hub on 8 May, with nothing in Tressia or at the Norrow border, and added that there may be scans they cannot see. Routing control's general notice has the Halvenmark to Tressia trunk running two to four days behind, but that is not specific to this parcel. Neither version is confirmed at my end. Please confirm the last physical location, whether delivery today is possible at all, and a realistic estimate. If the page is wrong, please say who corrects it. The recipient took a day's leave on the strength of that page, has been in since early morning and held for fifty minutes without getting an answer, so please reply today. I have told him nothing about timing.

rationale: The page says today and the only scan anyone has read out is four days old and two countries back, but the care line agent admitted they may not see every scan. The desk cannot settle that, and Routing control named Parcel trace team as the team that can. Reading the page back, or announcing that it is not coming, both pick a side on a fact the desk has not confirmed.

review.note: Blind answer puts the page-versus-scan conflict to Parcel trace team by Email and asks for an answer today; the must item no longer requires mentioning the fifty-minute hold.
